data.title: Default or Weak Service Credentials
data.summary:
Multiple internal services were accessible using default or trivially guessable
credentials, granting immediate administrative access to database and
application management interfaces.
data.description:
Several services exposed on the internal network were configured with vendor
default credentials or with passwords that were trivially guessable. These
accounts held administrative privileges within their respective applications.

In the case of database services, administrative access also permitted
operating system command execution through built-in functionality such as the
MSSQL xp_cmdshell extended stored procedure, turning application-level access
into host-level compromise.
data.impact:
An attacker with network access to these services could authenticate as an
administrator without any prior credential material. Where the affected service
runs under a privileged account, this results in code execution on the underlying
operating system, compromise of the data the service holds, and a foothold from
which the wider domain can be attacked.
data.recommendation:
1. Change all default and weak credentials immediately to values meeting the
   organisation's password standard, with a minimum of 15 random characters for
   service accounts.

2. Where the service supports it, disable or rename built-in default accounts
   rather than only changing their password.

3. Disable dangerous built-in functionality that is not required for operation,
   including the MSSQL xp_cmdshell extended stored procedure.

4. Restrict network access to management interfaces to dedicated administrative
   networks using host and network firewall rules.

5. Introduce a build review process that verifies default credentials have been
   changed before any system is placed into production.
